correctness.rationale: An independent coordinate derivation starts at the centroid and takes the three vectors to the midpoints of the edges incident to one vertex. Inverting these midpoint identities gives the four even-minus sign patterns in those vectors. Each opposite-edge equality makes a pair of the vectors orthogonal, and nondegeneracy makes all three lengths positive. Conversely the edge-square triple is four times the three pairwise sums of squared semiaxes, so the sorted axes determine the similarity class. The origin has equal vertex distances and equal perpendicular distances to the four faces (the omitted vertex has signed axial-coordinate sum 3, and all other vertices have sum -1), giving the exact circumradius and inradius. At fixed E, the resulting inverse squared roundness is a constant plus (1+E^-2)(z+E²/z) with z=t² in [1,E²]. This is strictly decreasing to z=E and then strictly increasing, and its values at z=1,E² agree. Thus both endpoints, all intermediate values, and precisely two distinct sorted-axis classes for each interior value follow; the two quadratic roots have product E². Each endpoint decreases strictly as E increases above 1; solving the two reciprocal quadratics gives the stated fixed-h interval. Expanding the endpoint equalities at E=1 gives deficits 4(E-1)²/27 and (E-1)²/9, respectively, hence the stated sharp inverse coefficients. At E=1 the only tetrahedron up to similarity is regular. The exact-rational checker was read, not executed; the proof is real-variable and algebraic. The displayed covering-radius specialization is algebraically correct conditional on the cited prior covering formula.

value.rationale: The extreme-axis ratio is an intrinsic geometrically motivated distortion parameter. The theorem gives exact global roundness bounds at a prescribed distortion, both lower equality classes, the non-isosceles upper shape for E>1, and the full inverse shape ambiguity and near-regular window. These supply quantitative information not present in an unconstrained radius formula; no significance is attributed merely to the rational test grid or to the previous covering result.
